main_text.p: הִתְפַּרְקוּ Abruperunt sibi, sive, Detraxerunt inaures aureas, Exod.32.24.
פֶּרֶק m. Diruptio, Dilaceratio, Lacetatum, Nah.3.1. At Obad.14. ab Hebraïs exponitur Compitum, quasi via Disruptio. Rabbini Caput libri sic vocant.
פֶּרֶק m. Fructum: Coinstr. פְּרַק פְּלִים וּפְרַק [?] Et fragmen sive Fructum carnium abominandarum, Jesa.65.4. pro quo legendum juxta Masoretbas, וּמֵרַק [?]. Vitæ מֵרְק [?].
מִפְרֶקֶת f. Cervix, Compages vertebrarum cervicis, à nodus & Interruptionibus sic dicta: Aff. אֶת־מִפְרַקְתּוֹ [?] Cervicem suam, 1.Sam.4.18.
פָּר פִּיר m. Cacabus, Num.11.8. בְּפָרוּר In cacabo, Jud.6.19. Cum epenthesi, פָּארוּר Nigror ol-laris, Pallor livens, juxta R.Salomonem, Joel.2.6. at juxta R.Aben Esram est à פָּאַר. Vide illic.

פָּרַשׁ Exposuit, Explanavit, Declaravit, Explicuit: Infinit. לְפָרֵשׁ לָהֶם Ad exponendum eis, Lev.24.12. Niph. נִפְרַשׁ Separari, Dispergi, Dispari. Particip. צֵאנוֹ נִפְרָשׁוֹת Ovium suarum dispersarum, Ezech.34.12. Pyh. Præteritum, פֹּרַשׁ Expositum fuit, Num.15.34. Particip. מְפֹרָשׁ Explanatum, loco adverbii, Explanatè, Nehem.8.8. Chald. מְפָרַשׁ Explicare; Esr.4.18. Hiph. ex alia significatione, Futurum, יַפְרִישׁ Pungeret, Prov.23.32.

פָּרָשׁ masc. Eques, quòd equum calcaribus (quæ & hinc פָּרָשִׁים Rabbinis dicuntur) Pungat, Nah.3.3. Ab. Esra scribit Prov.23.32. פָּרָשׁ dicitur בַּעֲבוּר הַפָּרָשִׁים אֲשֶׁר בְּרַגְלָיו à calcaribus quæ sunt in pedibus ejus. Et in Pathach, פָּרָשׁ Equitum, Ezech.26.10. ex forma dagessata, פָּנִ־שׁ [?]; Plural. פָּרָשִׁים Equites, Gen.50.9. Aff. וּפָרָשָׁיו Et equitibus suis, Jesa.28.28. Kimchi, Cuspidibus sive Dentibus illius, scil. הַחָרוּ [?] Tribula, quæ sunt acuta & pungentes.

page.notes: The Hebrew at the head of several entries (the Frustum entry, the Cervix entry, the Pathach example and the Tribula entry) is only partly legible on the scan. Those words are marked [?] and should be checked against a clearer image. "Lacetatum" is printed so; it is probably "Lacceratum" or "Laceratum" and is left as printed. "Sic" at the foot is an editorial remark, set apart from the text. No running head is printed on this page.
